description:
FILED s484d (2026-09-14).  t/op/anonsub.t produced 6 rows until this session
(#1652); it now runs all 15 of perl's, 6 passing.  Of the 9 failures, FOUR are
already-blessed principle-9 rows (`'sub;' is illegal` and its three siblings:
PCL does not reject invalid perl -- docs/not-supported.md "Error compatibility
for invalid Perl input"), and one is perl's own TODO row.  The rest:

  * record 4 -- `sub X; sub X { my $n = "ok 1\n"; eval 'sub Y {...}'; Y(sub {
    print $n }) }`.  PCL's child prints the answer AND an SBCL style-warning
    block ("undefined function: main::pl-Y"), because the sub defined inside
    the string eval is not visible to the compilation of the enclosing sub.
    The warning text is #1773 (it should never reach the compared output);
    whether the CALL then works is the real question -- measured, the child
    does print `ok 1`, so this row fails ONLY on the noise.  Re-measure it
    after #1773.
  * records 6 and 7 -- "Useless use of anonymous subroutine in void context"
    and its sibling: warnings-gated diagnostics are absent
    (docs/not-supported.md, owner #221).
  * row 9 `undef &anon giving it a freed GV` -- perl's answer after `undef
    &$anon` is a specific `__ANON__` rendering.

So this file's honest residue is small and two thirds of it belongs to #1773
and #221.
subject: op/anonsub.t's 4 record rows: a sub defined in a STRING EVAL is not visible to the enclosing compilation, and __ANON__/freed-GV naming
